questions.q: What is the capstone project scoped in this lesson?
options: A two-report paginated report suite: a summary report that drills through into a detail report
A single standalone chart with no parameters
A rewrite of Lesson 1's web portal screenshot
A subscription schedule with no reports attached to it
questions.explain: The capstone is a real report suite: a summary report and a detail report, linked by a drillthrough action and both driven by parameters.

questions.q: Which database does the summary report's dataset query?
options: AdventureWorksDW2014, using FactInternetSales, DimSalesTerritory, and DimDate
AdventureWorks2012, using Sales.SalesOrderHeader directly
A brand-new database created just for this capstone
No database — the summary report uses hardcoded values
questions.explain: The summary report is built on the warehouse-style AdventureWorksDW2014 database, joining the internet sales fact table to the territory and date dimensions.

questions.q: What column bridges the summary report's warehouse data to the detail report's transactional data?
options: DimSalesTerritory.SalesTerritoryAlternateKey, which preserves the original TerritoryID from AdventureWorks2012
FactInternetSales.SalesAmount
Production.Product.Name
There is no shared column — the two reports are unrelated
questions.explain: SalesTerritoryAlternateKey carries the original OLTP TerritoryID into the warehouse unchanged, which is exactly what a drillthrough action needs to pass as a parameter into the detail report's AdventureWorks2012 query.

questions.q: Which three tables does the detail report's dataset query, and from which database?
options: Sales.SalesOrderHeader, Sales.SalesOrderDetail, and Production.Product, from AdventureWorks2012
DimSalesTerritory, DimDate, and DimProduct, from AdventureWorksDW2014
FactInternetSales alone, from AdventureWorksDW2014
Three tables the student must design from scratch with no fixed schema
questions.explain: The detail report queries the same OLTP order tables this catalog's T-SQL course already queries directly: SalesOrderHeader, SalesOrderDetail, and Product.

questions.q: According to the Dataset -> Layout -> Parameters -> Drillthrough architecture, when does Lesson 39 build all four pieces?
options: All four, for both reports, in one lesson
One piece per lesson across four separate lessons
Only the Dataset piece — the rest is deferred indefinitely
Drillthrough is built first, before any dataset exists
questions.explain: Because this chapter only has three lessons, Lesson 39 builds the dataset, layout, parameters, and drillthrough for both reports in one sitting; Lesson 40 then evaluates the finished result.
